changes: original_meaning 与法语 (voiture) omnibus 的字面义对齐为「为所有人乘坐的（马车）」，并写明其拉丁语素（omnibus = omnis 的与格复数『为所有人』）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（1829 年公共马车、1835 年『包罗多案』形容词义、合集义），how 写明从车辆名到汇编义的桥。
evidence: Etymonline: "omnibus (n.) 1829, \"long-bodied, four-wheeled public vehicle with seats for passengers,\" from French (voiture) omnibus \"(carriage) for all, common (conveyance),\" from Latin omnibus \"for all,\" dative plural of omnis \"all\"... Introduced by Jacques Lafitte in Paris in 1819 or '20, used in London from 1829."
Etymonline: "As an adjective, in reference to legislation, \"designed to cover many different cases, embracing numerous distinct objects,\" recorded from 1835"
Oxford: "early 19th cent.: via French from Latin, literally 'for all', dative plural of omnis."
omnibus.mechanism_sentence: omnibus 是拉丁语「为所有人」：1819 年巴黎跑起来的公共马车就挂这个名——谁出钱谁能坐；后来「什么都往里装」又长出了法案、书刊的「合集」义。

semantic_path.how: 名字随实物出口：1829 年这种长车身公共马车开进伦敦，omnibus 随之进入英语专指它（后来缩成 bus）；马车换成汽车，词义守着『人人可乘的公共车辆』——词库今义『公共汽车』即此。
形容词先迈出这一步：1835 年起 omnibus 形容法案『一案包罗多事』；名词随后添『一卷收多作』的合集义（词库义）——从『为所有人』滑到『把所有的装在一起』，靠的是『全』这个老核（转喻引申）。

changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 ōra 的 gloss「未加工的金属」，与首站对齐。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明 ōra 与 ār 两词 17 世纪合流的史实（Etymonline），替换套话——本词的『变化』本质是词形合流，来源有明确交代。
evidence: Etymonline: "ore (n.) \"a metalliferous mineral or rock,\" especially one worth mining, 12c., a merger of Old English ora \"ore, unworked metal\"... and Old English ar \"brass, copper, bronze\"... The two words were not fully assimilated till 17c.; what emerged has the regular modern form of ar but the meaning of ora."
Oxford: "Old English ōra 'unwrought metal', of West Germanic origin; influenced in form by Old English ār 'bronze'"
ore.mechanism_sentence: 现代 ore 是两个古英语词合流的产物：ōra「矿石」贡献了意思，ār「铜、青铜」贡献了形状，两个词长得像、意思挨着，17 世纪彻底合成了一个。

semantic_path.how: 这是一个『合流词』：古英语 ōra（矿石）与 ār（黄铜、青铜）音近义近，几百年里越靠越拢，17 世纪彻底并成一个词——留下了 ār 的拼写骨架，装着 ōra 的词义（Etymonline）。此后 ore 专指值得开采的矿石，词库今义即此。

changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 ōþer 的「第二的；另一个」双义。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明『第二』义被 second 接管、脱落的史实（Etymonline），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "other (adj., pron.) Old English oþer \"second, the second of two; additional, further\" (adj.), also as a pronoun, \"one of the two; a different person or thing from the one in view\""

Etymonline: "The sense of \"second\" was detached from this word in English (which now uses second (adj.), which is from Latin) and German (zweiter, from zwei \"two\") to avoid ambiguity. In Scandinavian, however, the second floor is still the \"other\" floor (Swedish andra, Danish anden)."
other.mechanism_sentence: other 在古英语里一身兼二职——「第二的、另一个」：后来「第二」被拉丁语来的 second 接管（免得歧义），other 就专心做「其他的」了；北欧语里同源词至今还兼着「第二」。

semantic_path.how: 『第二』义被摘走了：为免歧义，英语改用源自拉丁语的 second 表示『第二』，other 从此专管『另一个、其他的』（Etymonline）；词库今义即此脱落后的词义。

changes: original_meaning 大改：现行字段「被拥有的」把词形关系译反；āhte 是 āgan『拥有』的过去式、且该词兼有『欠』义。按 Etymonline 改为「（过去）拥有，欠」。
semantic_path 重建两站，how 写明『欠债→欠义务→应当』的语义桥与 12 世纪末助动词义、17 世纪与 owe 分家的编年。
evidence: Etymonline: "ought (v.) Old English ahte \"owned, possessed,\" past tense of agan \"to own, possess; owe\" (see owe). As a past tense of owe, it shared in that word's evolution and meant at times in Middle English \"possessed\" and \"under obligation to pay.\" It has been detached from owe since 17c.... As an auxiliary verb expressing duty or moral obligation (the main modern use, attested from late 12c.), it represents the past subjunctive."
Wiktionary: "from Old English āgan 'to own, possess'"
ought.mechanism_sentence: ought 是 owe 的老亲戚：古英语 āgan 一词兼着「拥有」和「欠」——欠钱的「欠」，后来升格成欠责任的「应当」；ought 用的正是它的过去虚拟式，12 世纪末起专门管「应该」。

semantic_path.how: 桥在『欠』字上：āgan 的『欠』从欠债滑向欠义务，ought 以它的过去虚拟式在 12 世纪末独立成助动词，专表道德义务『应该』；17 世纪起与 owe 正式分家（Etymonline 编年）——金钱债的『欠』升成了道义上的『应当』。
